categoryBlurb.connection: A loading-zone boundary between two maps — crossing it streams you to the far side.
categoryBlurb.site-of-grace: Resting at a site of grace will restore your HP, FP, and cleanse any status ailments. It will also refill your sacred flasks. However, most of the enemies you've defeated will be revived.
categoryBlurb.spiritspring: Jump while on horseback near a spiritspring to ride its current high into the air. You won't take damage from jumping into a spiritspring while on horseback, even from a great height.
categoryBlurb.stake-of-marika: Upon dying, you will be revived at the last site of grace that you visited. However, if there is a Stake of Marika near where you died, you can choose to be revived there instead.
categoryBlurb.summon-pool: In each area, you may find effigies of martyrs. These effigies are summoning pools. You'll find it easy to summon other players at these locations, as co-op and hostile summoning signs created with small effigies gather at summoning pools.
categoryBlurb.summon-sign: With a Spirit Calling Bell, you can use ashes to summon various spirits. Summoning typically consumes FP.
categoryBlurb.teardrop-scarab: There are both Crimson and Cerulean Teardrop Scarabs. Defeat them to replenish the flasks that match their type.
categoryBlurb.waygate: A waygate. Step through to be teleported to its linked gate.

onboarding.step_welcome_body: Interactive maps, bosses and items for Elden Ring & Nightreign. Here's a quick tour of the essentials.
onboarding.step_world_body: Toggle between Elden Ring and Nightreign, then pick the region or map layer you want to explore.
onboarding.step_seed_body: Pick your Nightlord, then find the matching map pattern — Shifting Earth, spawns and night bosses all resolve from it.
onboarding.step_filters_body: Choose which markers show on the map — bosses, items, NPCs and more — so you see only what you need.
onboarding.step_search_body: Jump straight to any location, item or boss. Pick a result and the camera flies you there.
onboarding.step_add-marker_body: Place custom pins anywhere on the map — routes, reminders, anything worth tracking.
onboarding.step_bookmarks_body: Star any location to build a personal shortlist you can jump back to in one click.
onboarding.step_patterns_body: Star the current pattern to keep it, then jump back to any saved run in a single click.
onboarding.step_nav-er_body: Switch between the live map and the Archive — the full, searchable item & boss database.
onboarding.step_nav-nr_body: Switch between the live map and the Nightfarers, Nightlords and Relics databases.
onboarding.step_menu_title: Everything else is in the menu
onboarding.step_menu_body: The Archive, Nightfarers, Nightlords, Relics, your account, language and settings all live behind this button.
onboarding.step_language_body: Switch the entire app to your language — the map, database and menus all follow instantly.
onboarding.step_settings_body: This is your control room. Let's step through what's inside — display options, shortcuts and more.
onboarding.step_settings-map_body: Group nearby markers to declutter the map, and scale marker icons up or down until they read just right.
onboarding.step_settings-shortcuts_body: Move with W/A/S/D, close panels with Esc, and click markers to open them — the fastest way around the map.
onboarding.step_settings-game_body: Choose whether the Atlas opens automatically when Elden Ring or Nightreign launches — the in-game corner map always appears.
onboarding.step_settings-hotkeys_body: Rebind the global hotkeys that toggle the Atlas window and the overlay map while you're in-game.
onboarding.step_settings-replay_body: Need a refresher later? Reopen this guided tour anytime from here — it's always one click away.
onboarding.step_account_body: Sign in to sync your bookmarks and progress across every device — free, and everything else works without it.
onboarding.step_finish_body: That's the tour. Dive in — and may the Erdtree guide your way.

nrEventDesc.Night Horde: A roaming horde of enemies sweeps the map this day. Clearing it is dangerous but yields extra runes and loot to power your team up before nightfall.
nrEventDesc.Meteor Strike: Meteors bombard a stretch of the map, scarring the terrain. The impact zone turns hazardous but can carve new routes and expose loot.
nrEventDesc.Morgott Invasion: Morgott, the Omen King, prowls the map as an elite roaming field boss. High risk — but bringing him down is a major power spike.
nrEventDesc.Extra Night Boss: An additional boss joins the night phase, raising the night's difficulty and its rewards alike.
nrEventDesc.Maris Bubbles: A Maris-themed hazard: drifting bubbles roam an area of the map, foreshadowing the Augur Nightlord. Contact risks Sleep build-up.
nrEventDesc.Frenzy Tower: A tower channels the Frenzied Flame, radiating madness build-up to anyone who lingers near it. Approach from range or move through quickly.
nrEventDesc.Gnoster Plague: A Gnoster-themed plague of pestilence spreads through a region — standing in it drains your health with poison and rot.
nrEventDesc.Libra Curse: A Libra-themed curse warps the balance of an area, applying the Equilibrious Beast's affliction to those caught inside.
nrEventDesc.Difficult Sorcerer's Rise: The map's Sorcerer's Rise hides a tougher puzzle and guardian than usual — solving it grants a stronger reward.
nrEventDesc.Walking Mausoleum: A Walking Mausoleum lumbers across the map. Bring down its legs and ring its bell to claim the boss reward sealed inside.
nrEventDesc.__fallback: A special twist unique to this expedition.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy — Elden Ring Atlas
privacy.description: How Elden Ring Atlas handles your data: what the website and the Overwolf app collect, which advertising and analytics partners are involved, and how to manage, export or delete your information.
privacy.heading: Privacy Policy
privacy.lead: Elden Ring Atlas is a fan-made companion for Elden Ring and Nightreign, available as a website and as an Overwolf app. This policy explains what we collect, why we collect it, who we share it with, and what you can do about it.

sections.title: What we collect
sections.body: Most of the Atlas works without an account. You only hand us personal data when you sign in, sync your progress, post a note, or contact support.

items.text: If you create an account, our authentication provider (Supabase) stores your email address and a securely hashed password. If you sign in with Google, it stores the email address linked to that Google account. We never see your Google password.

Markers you tick off, bookmarks, custom pins, favourite Nightreign map patterns and any character stats you enter. With an account these sync to our database so they follow you between devices; without one they stay on your device only.
Notes, likes and reports you post are public and appear under the display name you choose. Choose a name you are comfortable showing publicly — you can change it at any time.
Messages you send through the in-app support form, together with the display name you provide and a random device identifier that lets us show you replies.

Which screens are opened, which features are used, your app version, your display setup and whether the game is running. These are aggregate product statistics used to decide what to build next — they are not sold and are not used to build advertising profiles.
On the website, our advertising partners may set and read cookies and similar identifiers, and may receive your IP address, approximate location, and device or browser information.

sections.title: Advertising and cookies
sections.body: The website is funded by advertising delivered through NitroPay and its demand partners, including Google. Depending on where you live and the choices you make, these partners may use cookies and similar technologies to measure and personalise the ads you see. In the EU, EEA and UK, personalised advertising runs only if you agree to it in the consent dialog shown on your first visit — you can reopen that dialog and change your answer at any time using the link at the bottom of this page. If you are a California resident, you can opt out of the sale or sharing of your personal information using the “Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information” link, also at the bottom of this page. The Overwolf app shows ads through Overwolf’s own advertising system, which is governed by Overwolf’s privacy policy rather than this one.

sections.title: How we use your data
sections.body: To sign you in and keep your saved progress in sync; to show and moderate Community Notes; to answer support messages; to understand which parts of the Atlas are actually used so we can improve them; to show advertising that keeps the site free; and to keep the service secure and free of abuse.

sections.title: Who we share it with
sections.body: We do not sell your personal information for money. We share only what each of these providers needs to do its job:

items.text: Accounts, authentication, saved progress, Community Notes and support threads.
Product analytics — which features are used, in aggregate.
Website hosting and basic page analytics.
Advertising delivery, measurement and, where consented, personalisation.
Distribution and advertising for the desktop app version.

sections.title: Your choices and rights
sections.body: Wherever you live, you can ask us for a copy of the personal data we hold about you, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it — including your whole account. Deleting your account removes your synced progress and support threads; Community Notes you posted are anonymised or removed. If you are in the EU, EEA or UK you also have the right to object to certain processing and to complain to your local data protection authority. To make any of these requests, contact us at the address below.

sections.title: Data retention
sections.body: Account data and saved progress are kept until you delete your account. Support threads are kept while they are open and for a reasonable period afterwards so we can follow up. Analytics events are retained in aggregate. Advertising cookies expire according to each partner’s own retention rules.

sections.title: Children
sections.body: The Atlas is a companion for games rated for mature audiences and is not directed at children under 13 (under 16 in the EEA and UK). We do not knowingly collect personal data from them. If you believe a child has given us data, contact us and we will delete it.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
sections.body: If this policy changes in a way that affects you, we will update the date at the top of this page and, for significant changes, say so in the app.

privacy.contactBody: Questions about this policy, or a request about your data? Email us at
privacy.choicesBody: These controls are provided by our advertising partner and appear when they apply to you: the consent dialog for visitors in the EU, EEA and UK, and the opt-out link for California residents.
privacy.disclaimer: Elden Ring Atlas is an unofficial fan project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by FromSoftware or Bandai Namco Entertainment.
